nodes.summary: If a simple graph $G$ is $q$-list-colorable, then $G$ is $q$-colorable, that is, it has a proper coloring with $q$ colors.
nodes.title: List-colorable graphs are colorable

nodes.summary: For every finite graph $G$ with choice number $\chi_\ell$ and all natural numbers $r$, $s$ with $1 \le r \le s \le \chi_\ell$, one has $\lambda_r / r \ge \lambda_s / s$, where $\lambda_t$ is the minimum, over all assignments of lists of exactly $t$ colours to the vertices, of the largest number of vertices of $G$ that can be properly coloured from their lists.
nodes.title: Iradmusa's partial list colouring conjecture

nodes.summary: There exist a finite graph $G$ with choice number $\chi_\ell$ and natural numbers $r$, $s$ with $1 \le r \le s \le \chi_\ell$ such that $\lambda_r / r < \lambda_s / s$, where $\lambda_t$ is the minimum, over all assignments of lists of exactly $t$ colours to the vertices, of the largest number of vertices of $G$ that can be properly coloured from their lists. So Iradmusa's partial list colouring conjecture fails.
nodes.title: The partial list colouring conjecture is false

nodes.summary: There exist a finite simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices whose choice number $q$ is positive, a natural number $t \le q$, and an assignment to each vertex $v$ of a list $L(v)$ of exactly $t$ colors, such that every set $S$ of vertices of $G$ whose induced subgraph has a proper coloring giving each vertex a color from its list satisfies $q|S| < tn$.
nodes.title: The partial list coloring conjecture is false

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices whose choice number $q$ is positive, let $t \le q$ be a natural number, and assign to each vertex $v$ a list $L(v)$ of exactly $t$ colors. Then there is a set $S$ of vertices of $G$ that is partially list-colorable from $L$ (the subgraph of $G$ induced by $S$ has a proper coloring giving each vertex a color from its list) and satisfies $tn \le q|S|$, that is,…
nodes.title: Albertson–Grossman–Haas partial list coloring conjecture

nodes.summary: A natural number $q$ is the choice number of a simple graph $G$ if $G$ is $q$-list-colorable but is not $r$-list-colorable for any $r < q$.
nodes.title: Choice number

nodes.summary: A simple graph $G$ is $q$-list-colorable if, for every set of colors and every assignment of a finite list $L(v)$ of at least $q$ colors to each vertex $v$, there is a proper coloring $c$ of $G$ with $c(v) \in L(v)$ for every vertex $v$.
nodes.title: List colorability

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a graph on a finite vertex set $V$, let $L$ assign to each vertex $v$ a finite list $L(v)$ of colours (natural numbers), and let $S \subseteq V$. A map $f : V \to \mathbb{N}$ is a proper $L$-colouring of $S$ when $f(v) \in L(v)$ for every $v \in S$ and $f(v) \ne f(w)$ for all adjacent $v, w \in S$.
nodes.title: Proper list colouring of a vertex subset

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph and assign to each vertex $v$ a finite list $L(v)$ of colors. A finite set $S$ of vertices is partially list-colorable from $L$ when the subgraph of $G$ induced by $S$ has a proper coloring $c$ with $c(v) \in L(v)$ for every $v \in S$. No colors are assigned to vertices outside $S$.
nodes.title: Partial list colorability

nodes.summary: For a graph $G$ on a finite vertex set and an assignment $L$ of a finite list $L(v)$ of natural-number colours to each vertex $v$, $\lambda_L$ is the largest $k$ such that some set of $k$ vertices of $G$ has a proper $L$-colouring.
nodes.title: Maximum number of list-colourable vertices

nodes.summary: For a graph $G$ on a finite vertex set and a natural number $t$, $\lambda_t$ is the minimum of $\lambda_L$ over all assignments $L$ of a list $L(v)$ of exactly $t$ natural-number colours to each vertex $v$, where $\lambda_L$ is the largest $k$ such that some set of $k$ vertices of $G$ has a proper $L$-colouring.
nodes.title: The partial list colouring number $\lambda_t$

nodes.summary: If a simple graph $G$ is $q$-list-colorable and $q \le r$, then $G$ is $r$-list-colorable.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of list colorability

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
